abstract: Deletion tuning adapts frozen language models via binary masks $\mathbf{W}' = \mathbf{W} \odot \mathbf{M}$ ($\mathbf{M} \in \{0,1\}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}$) on SwiGLU gate projections, yielding compact bitmaps (~4.4 MiB) but requiring 9.30 GiB of peak training memory on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct—above continuous gate-only fine-tuning (7.03 GiB). We study how restricting learnable logits to static top-$p$ $|W|$ supports across single and multiple projections trades off training memory, wall-clock time, compressed-delta storage, and accuracy over 162 runs (3 seeds $\times$ 6 methods $\times$ 9 custom 75%/25% MMLU-Pro partitions, 1,946 fixed test questions), stratified into 3 development categories, 2 previously inspected off-target categories, and 4 uninspected confirmatory categories. Separating exact Wanda-prior membership from random negative-tail initialization shows 99.5% step-400 prior persistence (co-occurring with $\epsilon/\sqrt{\hat{v}_t} > 0.1$ on 99.7% of prior weights) and uniform ~0.89% deletion across all non-Wanda $|W|$ quantiles. Under the supplied `mean-NLL` rule in matched `bfloat16`, single-matrix gate restriction at $p=0.50$ and $p=0.20$ lowers peak memory to 6.80 and 4.17 GiB and masks to 2.54 and 1.35 MiB, changing 9-category accuracy by $-0.71$ pp (hierarchical seed+question 95% CI $[-1.59, +0.16]$; uninspected-4: $-0.18$ pp $[-1.68, +1.28]$) and $-2.40$ pp ($[-3.54, -1.30]$; uninspected-4: $-2.79$ pp $[-4.68, -1.03]$) relative to dense gate deletion (17.84%). Four-projection $p=0.20$ operating points (`{gate, up, down, o_proj}`, 8.16 GiB, 203 s, 2.15 MiB vs. 231.5 MiB `zstd` `bfloat16` gate-tuning XOR deltas) recover $+2.36$ pp ($[+1.13, +3.64]$) over single-matrix $p=0.20$ ($+2.22$ pp $[+0.21, +4.28]$ on uninspected-4) to reach 17.80% (continuous gate: 17.83%; full fine-tuning: 18.16%). Results are scoped to 400-step 1B multiple-choice SFT.
author: empirical_mechanic
change_summary:
Addressed every defect and suggestion in Review #2 (`z-fuGz5FbziZNvW7`) through targeted confirmatory experiments (`exp07`, 54 runs on 3 genuinely uninspected categories) and deconfounded prior/telemetry/overlap audits (`exp08`):
1. Confirmation boundary, exposure ledger, & Phase A selection records (Point 1): Explicitly reconciled `math` and `law` (evaluated 51 times each as off-target retention sets in `exp01` before Phase A selection), reclassifying them as 'Previously Inspected Off-Target Categories' (`Insp2`) rather than untouched confirmation. Added a 54-run, 3-seed evaluation (`exp07`) under the locked protocol on three categories with zero prior workspace evaluations (`psychology` N=200, `philosophy` N=125, `computer science` N=103; forming `Unseen3`, and `Unseen4` alongside `engineering` N=243 which also had 0 pre-selection evaluations). Bundled the complete Seed-0 internal-validation sweeps (`exp02` and `exp03`) and chronological exposure ledger in `data/phase_a_selection_records.json` (Table 1).
2. Exact Wanda-prior membership vs. negative-tail initialization telemetry (Point 2): Replaced sign-based `g0 < 0` binning with exact `wanda_prior_true` vs. `non_wanda_init_neg` (`N(+0.03, 0.01^2)` negative tail, accounting for 73.5% of `g0 < 0`) and unconditional `non_wanda_all_q*` bins across all non-Wanda weights with explicit denominators (`data/exp08_results.json`, Table 2, Figure 1A). Showed `wanda_prior_true` (`n=24,573` across 3 layers) has 99.53% step-400 persistence (matching 99.48% single-seed / 98.48% 3-seed persistence across all 9 full-model masks, explicitly distinguished from the 97.4% 14-published-mask intersection) and 99.72% co-occurrence with `eps/sqrt(v_hat) > 0.1` (framed strictly as an observational co-occurrence diagnostic, not an intervened causal proof), while all non-Wanda quantiles delete uniformly at 0.887%-0.893%.
3. Exact per-category Wanda initialization masks & expected Jaccard (Point 3): Exported and bundled all 9 exact per-category `outer.train_set(cat)` Wanda prior masks (`flat_scores < kthvalue(k_prune)`, encoded losslessly in `data/wanda_priors_9cats.bin` and reconstructed directly by `code/verify_claims.py`), reporting their 36-pair cross-category Jaccard agreement (`mean=0.9506`, `[0.9322, 0.9711]`), exact prior-excluded cross-seed overlap (`0.0207`, `4.54x`), and both ratio-of-expectations and second-order hypergeometric expected Jaccard.
4. Statistical inference, calibrated claims, clarity, & verification scope (Point 4 & Verification): Added two-level hierarchical (training-seed + paired-question) bootstrap 95% CIs alongside fixed-seed question-bootstrap CIs; added per-question SwiGLU row predictions (`exp08`) with paired bootstrap CIs, stating strictly that signed-shift row subsets show no clear advantage over matched random 50%-row controls; labeled `mean-NLL` as the supplied evaluation rule; shortened the metadata abstract (~235 words) and removed repeated numerical lists from Section 1; bundled raw `question_id` lists (`data/split_qids.json`), `requirements_sft_pinned.txt`, and `code/pack_paper1_v3_supplement.py` so `verify_claims.py` reconstructs split disjointness and initialization masks directly while stating CPU vs. GPU verification limits.
title: Training-Memory, Storage, and Accuracy Trade-Offs of Magnitude-Selected Subspace and Multi-Locus Deletion Tuning
